Later years fall back as the Gulf disruption normalises, then recover only modestly as fleet additions add earning days.

quotes.quote: long-run nominal growth anchor g_anchor 0.0375

terminal_growth.why: A fleet-based shipping business grows with trade and replacement pricing, not above the long-run nominal anchor. I use 0.03, below the 0.0375 anchor, because the business is cyclical and fleet-capacity-limited.

risks.risk: The Persian Gulf disruption ends quickly and rates fall below mid-cycle, with newbuild deliveries adding supply, so margins settle below the historical median.
Spot rates on open days and the 2027 contract book fall sharply once the conflict-driven inefficiencies fall away, so Year 2 revenue drops more than assumed.
Newbuilding commitments, bought at peak-cycle prices, earn less than expected and push up capital intensity.

debt_level_representative.why: Net loan-to-value of 25.9% is low and total borrowings were 1,137.8m at 30 September 2026, but the newbuilding pipeline through 2030 will probably need more debt.

situation.margin_position: The FY2025 margin of 0.266 is near the company's own multi-year median (about 0.27). FY2026 is far above it: nine-month EBIT was 709m on revenue of 1,564m, and the company says the strength comes from US-Iran conflict disruption to oil flows. Year 1 therefore sits at a cycle peak, and I fade it back toward the median.

tax_rate_representative.why: The base-year tax rate of 0.0312 (tax of 9.2 on pretax profit of 295.2) is consistent with low tax across 2023-2026, and the nine-month 2026 tax charge was only 3.0 on 662.8.

situation.why: FY2025 is a mid-cycle year and Year 1 (FY2026) is a spike. 88% of FY2026 earning days were fixed at USD/day 50,487, and Q4 is partly covered at USD/day 78,419. Both are well above what I would assume holds in later years. Revenue history swings from 619.5m to 1,559.2m, so the base year alone says little about 2026, and the peak should not be extrapolated.

situation.why: FY2025 revenue of $1,339.5m and EBIT of $356.3m are well below the 2026 run-rate, because 2026 is an exceptional rate spike with 9M EBIT of USD 709m. The long-run margin is anchored near the company's own long-run median rather than the peak.

financial_health.claim: The going concern assessment states sufficient liquidity and covenant headroom in the base case, and also in a reverse stress case, through 31 March 2027.
quotes: In the base case, TORM has sufficient liquidity and headroom for all the covenant limits.

In the reverse stress case, with TCE rates significantly below the lowest rolling four-quarter average observed since 2000 on each vessel class basis accompanied by a corresponding decline in vessel values, TORM maintains sufficient headroom on liquidity and covenants throughout the going concern period.

quotes: Subsequent to quarter-end, TORM entered into agreements for eight LR2 newbuildings to be held through a 50/50 joint venture structure, and secured options for an additional two MR newbuildings.

growth_thesis.claim: Third-quarter TCE earnings rose to USD 353m from USD 236m a year earlier, and the company attributes the strength to oil trade disruptions from the US-Iran conflict.
quotes: In the third quarter of 2026, TORM (Nasdaq: TRMD or TRMD A) generated time charter equivalent earnings (TCE) of USD 353m (2025, same period: USD 236m).
During the quarter, tanker freight markets were supported by continued disruptions to global oil trade flows stemming from the conflict involving the US and Iran.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in P1; linking it to the Q3 driver is inferred
growth_thesis.claim: For the freight-rate driver to continue, the geopolitical disruption must persist; the company's going-concern base case assumes it will.
quotes: TORM’s base case assumes that these dynamics will persist.

growth_thesis.claim: Growth in the quarter came from both rate and volume: fleet-wide TCE per day rose to USD/day 40,102 from USD/day 31,012, and available earning days rose to 8,799 from 7,859.
quotes: In this market, TORM achieved fleet-wide TCE rates of USD/day 40,102 on average (2025, same period: USD/day 31,012), and available earning days increased to 8,799 (2025, same period: 7,859).

growth_thesis.basis: stated in P2; the link to earning days is inferred
growth_thesis.claim: Fleet additions support earning-day growth: six MR resale vessels were acquired, six MR newbuildings were ordered, and options for two more were exercised.
quotes: Following the acquisition of six MR resale vessels during the second quarter and the previously announced order of six MR newbuildings during the third quarter, TORM exercised options for an additional two MR newbuildings.

growth_thesis.claim: After quarter-end the company agreed to eight further newbuildings through a joint venture, and it describes a delivery pipeline running through 2030.
quotes: Subsequent to quarter-end, TORM entered into agreements for eight LR2 newbuildings to be held through a 50/50 joint venture structure, and secured options for an additional two MR newbuildings.

Collectively, these investments establish a significant pipeline of future fleet deliveries through 2030, reinforcing TORM's commitment to a modern and efficient fleet while supporting future earnings growth and long-term shareholder value creation.

growth_thesis.claim: Full-year TCE guidance was raised to USD 1,750 - 1,900m, from an original range of USD 1,400 – 1,600m before the October upgrade.
quotes: Thus, full-year 2026 TCE is now expected to be in the range of USD 1,750 - 1,900m, compared with USD 1,700 - 1,900m following the guidance upgrade announced on 12 October 2026.

TORM now expects full-year 2026 TCE to be in the range of USD 1,700 – 1,900m and full-year 2026 EBITDA to be in the range of USD 1,300 – 1,500m, compared to previous guidance of TCE of USD 1,400 – 1,600m and EBITDA of USD 1,000 – 1,200m.

growth_thesis.claim: Continued strength requires open-market rates to hold: 4,060 days remain open, and each USD/day 1,000 change moves EBITDA by about USD 4m.

A change in freight rates of USD/day 1,000 will, all else equal, impact EBITDA by approximately USD 4m.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in P2; the persistence condition is inferred
growth_thesis.claim: Supply tightness also drives rates: large tankers shifting into dirty trades cut clean-product carrying capacity by around 4%. This must persist to keep supporting earnings.
quotes: This effectively reduced CPP-carrying capacity by around 4% compared with the start of the year, adding another layer of supply-side tightness and supporting LR2 earnings at levels significantly above historical norms throughout the quarter.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in P2 as management outlook
growth_thesis.claim: The company argues that normalizing Gulf crude flows and a later inventory restocking cycle could support product tanker demand. This requires clean-product exports to rebound and inventories to be rebuilt.
quotes: Normalizing crude volumes from the Persian Gulf mean higher feedstock availability for refineries globally and thereby create a foundation for a rebound in clean product exports.

The resulting restocking cycle could provide a meaningful additional source of tanker demand and ton-miles, particularly if inventories are rebuilt beyond the levels prevailing before the Iran conflict.

growth_thesis.claim: Recovery in clean product flows has lagged: Persian Gulf product exports stayed below half of pre-conflict levels during the quarter.
quotes: The recovery in clean petroleum product (CPP) flows has been considerably slower.

Persian Gulf product exports remained below half of pre-conflict levels during the quarter, although an increasing share of the volumes that did move also relied on shuttle operations, involving close to 20 LR2 vessels.
